grid.title: {rect} rectifier {filt}
grid.unknown: the ripple factor and the DC output of a {rect} rectifier {filt}

rect.label: Half-wave
rect.note: One diode passes one half of every cycle, so the average is V_p/pi and the ripple comes at the mains frequency.

rect.label: Full-wave centre-tap
rect.note: Two diodes and the transformer's centre tap pass both halves, so the average doubles and the ripple comes at twice the mains frequency.

rect.label: Bridge
rect.note: Four diodes pass both halves without needing a centre tap, at the cost of two diode drops in the path at any instant.

source.title: J. Millman and C. C. Halkias, Integrated Electronics, chapter on rectifiers and filters; silicon diode forward drop taken as 0.7 V (1N4007)

filt.label: with a 470 microfarad filter
filt.note: 470 microfarad is an E6 preferred value; the time constant R_L C decides how far the capacitor discharges between peaks.

source.title: IEC 60063 preferred values (E6 series) for the capacitor; J. Millman and C. C. Halkias, Integrated Electronics, capacitor-filter analysis

filt.label: with a 1000 microfarad filter
filt.note: Doubling the capacitance roughly halves the ripple, at the price of a larger surge when the supply is first switched on.

source.title: IEC 60063 preferred values (E6 series) for the capacitor; J. Millman and C. C. Halkias, Integrated Electronics, capacitor-filter analysis
